business_problem: TapTap's ad-driven recommendation, search, and content workflows depended on machine-learning models and NLP processing, but the older ECS-plus-Rundeck environment made deployments and service management too slow and expensive. The team needed a more elastic platform for automated model updates, experiment tracking, content parsing, and online estimation services while continuing to support Go-based services and fast release cycles for a globally used game community.
solution_summary: XD moved TapTap's algorithm platform toward an all-on-serverless design using Function Compute (FC) and Serverless Application Engine (SAE). Model artifacts exported into OSS buckets trigger FC deployment workflows, so TensorFlow, PyTorch, and similar models can be published without separate engineering handoffs. An internal experiment-management service also runs on FC with HTTP triggers, recording training parameters and log addresses so model experiments stay traceable. New user posts are pushed through Kafka to an NLP parsing service, where event-driven execution invokes analysis only when content arrives and stores the results for later search use. The team also schedules FC jobs to pull unstructured billing data and aggregate MaxCompute and EAS consumption by task and model. On the serving side, SAE hosts shared estimation services used by search, recommendation, and advertising workloads, giving TapTap faster releases, microservice support, and lower operations overhead.

solution_components.name: Function Compute (FC)
solution_components.role: Runs TapTap's event-driven model deployment, experiment-management, NLP parsing, and scheduled cost-statistics workflows.

solution_components.name: Object Storage Service (OSS)
solution_components.role: Stores exported model artifacts whose arrival triggers automated deployment and update jobs.

solution_components.name: Kafka
solution_components.role: Streams newly created content into the NLP parsing workflow for downstream search enrichment.

solution_components.name: MaxCompute
solution_components.role: Provides a source for scheduled resource-consumption analysis tied to model and task cost management.

solution_components.name: Elastic Algorithm Service (EAS)
solution_components.role: Supplies algorithm-service resource signals that are aggregated for model-cost monitoring and management.

solution_components.name: Serverless Application Engine (SAE)
solution_components.role: Hosts the online estimation and microservice layer shared across search, recommendation, and advertising workloads.

data_flow: Model artifacts are written to OSS and trigger FC-based deployment jobs, experiment submissions arrive through HTTP-triggered FC services that log parameters and log locations, and new user posts are pushed through Kafka into event-driven NLP analysis for search indexing. Processed signals and online prediction services are then served through SAE, while scheduled FC tasks aggregate MaxCompute and EAS consumption data for internal cost control.
business_outcome: TapTap gave its algorithm engineers a faster, lower-ops platform for model deployment, NLP enrichment, and online estimation. The serverless design let the company decouple triggering logic from business code, reduce infrastructure management, and support faster releases and elastic scaling for recommendation and advertising services that affect user experience and monetization.
architecture_clues: OSS-triggered model deployment lets algorithm engineers publish models without a separate manual deployment path.
Kafka-triggered NLP analysis is invoked per new post so the platform can align cost with content volume.
Scheduled FC jobs aggregate MaxCompute and EAS resource usage by task and model to improve cost transparency.
SAE is used for shared estimation services that support search, recommendation, and advertising scenarios.
